title: Zenith customer — autoscale sweep and GPU economics (workshop notes)
body:
Purpose:
Run notes from the 2024-11-06 workshop with Zenith infra/product teams. Goal: establish a defensible autoscale policy and a cost/throughput baseline for a Dedicated GPU pool that will serve a multi-tenant LLM feature (customer-facing chat + background embedding jobs). This document captures assumptions, the synthetic traffic sweep we ran, policy recommendations, and an emergency scale/runbook for SRE handoff.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Zenith's steady-state is low (0.7 rps median) but has short, high-amplitude bursts tied to marketing events and hourly batch embedding windows. Simulations show a 3x peak multiplier over the 99th percentile sustained for 10–15 minutes is realistic. Using a mixed pool (A100 x4 equivalent + prewarmed A10G hot-standbys) with a target_utilization of 65% and a 120s cooldown gives the best cost/latency tradeoff in our sims — roughly 22–28% lower cost vs aggressive prewarming and 15–18% lower tail latency vs minimal warmup. Recommendation: initial commit to a reserved pool sized for the 95th percentile plus a 20% burst reserve and a scheduled autoscale policy (scheduled prewarm + reactive scale with cooldown).

Assumptions used in sims (explicit):
- Model family: 13B decoder-only open model (quantized pathway available). Benchmarks from serving-runtime: H100 (mixed precision) ~700 token/s, A100 ~420 token/s, A10G ~140 token/s for single-request streaming on 2k context. Embedding throughput assumed: 350 queries/s per A10G equivalent.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 400ms for chat small requests (<=128 tokens).
- Batch size: chat requests mostly single-user streaming, batchable up to 8; embeddings batched up to 128.
- Token mix: chat 80% short (<64 tokens), 15% medium (64–256), 5% long (>256).
- Traffic patterns: diurnal baseline with spike multiplier events up to 6x instantaneous for <3 minutes during marketing pushes.
- Pricing (on-prem/reserved amortized equivalent): H100 $18/hr, A100 $9/hr, A10G $2.8/hr — these are internal normalized rates for economics modeling, not cloud list prices.

Workload profile collected during the discovery call:
- Median qps: 0.7 requests/s
- 95th percentile qps: 12 requests/s (bursty windows)
- Embedding batch window: every hour, 30k items over 8 minutes (bursty background load)
- SLA requirement for peak business flows: <500ms 95th for chat customer flows

Simulation design (how we swept):
- Inputs: traffic traces (synthetic diurnal + injected marketing spikes), per-GPU throughput curves, queueing model for request arrival.
- Variables swept: pool_size, min_prewarm, scale_step (how many GPUs to add per autoscale action), cooldown_seconds, target_utilization, prioritized-queue thresholds (chat vs embeddings).
- Outputs measured: 95/99 latency percentiles, dropped requests (fail-open fallback), cost per hour, cold-start penalty (ms).
- Runs: 48h simulated windows with 30 randomized spike injections to capture tail behavior.

Key findings (high level):
- Very small min_prewarm (0–1 GPUs) with aggressive reactive scaling yields high 99th latency due to cold-starts for chat flows; improving min_prewarm to ~10% of peak significantly reduces tails at modest cost.
- Scheduled prewarm timed to hourly embedding windows cuts embedding-induced tail by 40% vs pure reactive scaling.
- For thin, steady chat loads, A10G-only pool is cost-optimal, but burst events degrade latency; mixed H100/A10G yields better tail characteristics with marginally higher amortized cost.
- Quantization to 4-bit reduces per-token cost ~28% but increases peak memory pressure; for Zenith's workload it's safe for embeddings and short chat but we advise rollback tests for long-form generation.

Representative sim outputs (selected scenarios):
- Scenario A: conservative pool (reserve = 95th +20% burst), target_util=65%, cooldown=120s, min_prewarm=2 GPUs (mixed). Result: 95th latency 320ms, 99th 540ms, cost = normalized $210/hr.
- Scenario B: minimal reserve, reactive-only, cooldown=30s, scale_step=1. Result: 95th latency 480ms, 99th 1.4s (many cold starts), cost = $170/hr (lower cost but poor SLA).
- Scenario C: scheduled prewarm aligned to embedding windows + burst guard. Result: embedding tail reduced 45%, chat 99th 560ms, cost = $235/hr.

Autoscale policy proposal (concrete):
- Pool composition: baseline mix = (1 x H100 equivalent per 8 A10G equivalents). Start with pool_size = 6 A10G-equivalents (mapped to 1 H100 + 2 A100 or equivalent) — adjust after one-week telemetry.
- Min_prewarm: 20% of expected peak concurrent GPUs (round up), always keep at least one hot H100-class node for latency-sensitive routing.
- Target_utilization: 60–70% for chat (prefer 65%). Embeddings use a lower target (40–50%) because they batch and can tolerate queueing.
- Scale_step: 2 GPU-equivalents for reactive upscales; 1 GPU-equivalent downscale step.
- Cooldown: 120s after upscale, 300s after downscale to avoid oscillation during marketing bursts.
- Prioritization: chat flows preempt embedding slots via a token-credit scheduler; embedding jobs have backpressure and scheduled prewarm windows.
- Fallbacks: automatically route to a smaller quantized model variant (13B-4bit) if queue depth > threshold or tail latency breaches SLA for > T seconds.

Operational runbook (short):
- Alerts: P95_latency_chat > 450ms for 5m, P99_latency_chat > 800ms for 1m, queue_depth > 50 for 2m. Pager to SE-on-call -> SRE.
- First response: verify pool usage and autoscale logs, confirm whether scale actions were attempted and if any failed (GKE/VM provisioning errors).
- Mitigation (fast): trigger manual scale up (+4 GPU-equivalents), enable fallback model routing, and if embeddings scheduled window active: pause non-critical batches.
- Postmortem trigger: any sustained P99 > 1s for >15 minutes or any customer-facing error.

Open questions and risks:
- Reserved commitment sizing: Zenith prefers a single 12-month reserved commitment if their traffic is stable — need finance calc to compare: commit for 70% of projected peak vs 95th. (Action: Ethan to run TCO of 70% commit vs 95% commit, JIRA-1234).
- GPU procurement lead time (private deployment) — if H100 procurement >8 weeks we must adjust policy to rely on A100/A10G mix earlier.
- Quantization regression risk for long-form outputs — need a small internal eval set from Zenith (action: Priya to collect 500 long-form prompts).

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Finalize reserved pool sizing sensitivity (Ethan Park) — due 2024-11-13 — JIRA-1234
- Provide Zenith an A/B test plan for quantized fallback (Priya Ramesh) — due 2024-11-15
- Implement scheduled prewarm job in pool-sim and attach telemetry (Oliver Smith) — PR in progress: linked above — due 2024-11-18
- One-week telemetry review after initial deployment (Marisol) — schedule follow-up workshop 2024-11-27

Appendix: quick math reference used in sims:
- H100 throughput (chat short): 700 t/s -> roughly 5–6 concurrent short chat windows per GPU at 128 token budget.
- A10G throughput (chat short): ~140 t/s.
- Embedding throughput: A10G-equivalent ~350 qps when batched.
- Normalized cost per A10G-equivalent-hour = $2.8; convert H100 -> 6x A10G-equivalents for economics.

Notes to self (informal):
- Zenith cares about predictable bills > absolute lowest cost. Emphasize predictability in next deck.
- Watch the long-chat regression when enabling 4-bit quantization; probably need a fallback route sooner than later.

Contact:

- SRE contact: Oliver Smith (oliver@redwood.example)

End of notes.
